 Dated this the 7th day of April, 2025  JUDGMENT Appellant and the 1st respondent are the children of a person named Chandran, who died in a motor accident on 25.01.2015.

The accident occurred at about 8:30 am on 21.01.2015, when the motor cycle in which the deceased was riding pillion and his son, the 1 st respondent was the rider, hit a divider and an electric post, resulting in the rider and the deceased falling on the road and sustaining injuries.
Although Chandran was rushed to the nearest hospital, he succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident four days later.
The accident allegedly occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of his motor cycle by the 1 st respondent.

As against a claim for Rs.20 lakhs raised by the appellant, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.7,84,600/- and found the Prameesha Chandran vs Praveen Chandran on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143307769/

The 1 st respondent, who is the other surviving legal heir of the deceased, was found disentitled for the compensation, he being the insured and the tortfeasor.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the Tribunal committed gross illegality in fixing the notional income of the deceased as Rs.7000/- per month, despite production of Ext.A7 salary certificate and Ext.A8 caste certificate.

It is submitted that the caste certificate was sufficient to prove that the deceased belonged to the Vishwakarma community and the salary certificate showed that, at the time of the accident, the deceased was working as a blacksmith in Marymatha Engineering, Chittissery on a monthly salary of Rs.24,000/-.
Reliance is placed on the decision of the Apex Court in Rajwati @ Rajjo v. United India Insurance Company Ltd.

to contend that the Motor Vehicles Act being a beneficial piece of legislation, strict rules of evidence as in a criminal trial are not applicable and the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of 2025:KER:32980 preponderance of probabilities.
It is also argued that the compensation of Rs.30,000/- granted towards pain and suffering is too meagre, the deceased having survived for four days, undergoing acute pain and suffering.
3. Learned counsel for the insurance company contended that, since just and fair compensation is ordered by the Tribunal, the award warrants no interference.

4. A perusal of the impugned award shows that the Tribunal had refused to accept the salary of the deceased as Rs.24,000/- per month, since Ext.A7 was not proved by examining the author of the document.
Here, it is essential to note that the insurer had not raised any serious dispute with regard to the avocation of the deceased.
On a reasonable assumption, the monthly income of a blacksmith in 2015 would be at Rs.15,000/-.

The deceased being aged 55 years at the time of his death, 10% of the income has to be added towards future prospects, as held in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v.
2025:KER:32980 Pranay Sethi and Others [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

6.
A perusal of the impugned award and the available materials reveals that the tribunal has granted reasonable and just compensation under the other heads.
Therefore, the compensation under the heads loss of dependency and loss of consortium alone are re-

Although learned counsel for the 1 st respondent contended that the tribunal grossly erred in denying compensation to one of the legal heirs on the premise that he is the insured, the said contention cannot be countenanced in the light of the settled legal position, discussed in detail in the impugned award.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed.
The appellant is found entitled to additional amount of Rs.4,07,200/-, towards his share of the enhanced compensation.
The amount granted towards enhanced compensation shall be paid to the appellant within three months, with interest @ 8% from the date of petition.
The MACA is disposed of accordingly.
